items.quote: significant investments in financial advisors and other human capital, technology infrastructure, digital initiatives, knowledge- and data-powered tools, and strategic relationships to support long-term growth objectives and deliver enhanced value and impact for millions of current and potential clients

items.text: Aboon CEO Nick Gavronsky states that the retirement plan management platform Edward Jones is developing will leverage Aboon Workplace, an AI-native platform that lets advisors find and win retirement plans all in one place, creating a simpler, more streamlined experience for advisors launching or scaling their retirement plan business.
items.quote: "RPMC will leverage Aboon Workplace, an AI-native platform that lets advisors find and win retirement plans all in one place," said Nick Gavronsky, Aboon CEO and co-founder

items.text: Kitces.com commentary questions Edward Jones's choice of Quicken for personal financial management and suggests Edward Jones could instead have bought Mint.com from Intuit or invested in a more modern platform such as Monarch Money.
items.quote: why not buy out Mint.com from Intuit just a few years ago before it was just outright shuttered (and ostensibly could have been had, in full, for far less than a partial stake in Quicken)? Or invest into a more modern platform solving the same "personal financial management" problem with modern tech, like Monarch Money
